branch_label: Identification is inadequate. No causal elasticity is claimed.
overidentification_test: not applicable; no instrument was approved
weak_instrument_diagnostics: not applicable; 2SLS was not estimated on the scanner rows
endogeneity_test: A Hausman test was not computed. It would require one estimator to be consistent for a causal parameter, and that estimator was not established.
ols_bias_direction: Not claimed. Pooled and fixed-effects slopes are different associations. Reading the gap as the sign of omitted-variable bias would require the fixed-effects slope to be the causal parameter.

instruments.source: Hoch, Drèze, and Purk 1994. Not a movement-file column.
instruments.construction: Not built. No store-category arm or cereal week window is on file.
instruments.rationale: Study 1 assigned stores, by category, to EDLP, Hi-Lo, or control.
instruments.exclusion: Usable only if the arm and the weeks are known and checked against prices.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Chainwide deals and a shared media market can move control stores.
instruments.common_shocks: Holidays, competitors, and chain advertising are citywide.
instruments.required_controls: Assignment and weeks, written down before any second stage.
instruments.verdict_reason: The assignment file is absent. A mined price pattern is not the trial.

instruments.source: Same movement row: PRICE, QTY, and PROFIT.
instruments.construction: log(unit price times (1 - PROFIT/100)) when that product is positive.
instruments.rationale: A wholesale cost could shift price if it were not built from that price.
instruments.exclusion: PROFIT is a sales margin, so this product puts the shelf price back in.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Forward buying ties wholesale deals to retail promotions.
instruments.required_controls: A cost that is not computed from the shelf price.
instruments.verdict_reason: This series is a function of retail price. An F statistic does not fix that.
instruments.cross_section_note: Same row as the shelf price.
instruments.time_note: Moves when the margin or the shelf price moves.

instruments.source: Same UPC-store series, previous calendar week only.
instruments.construction: Log unit price in week t-1 when that adjacent log-sample week exists.
instruments.rationale: A lag is predetermined on the calendar.
instruments.exclusion: Predetermined is not exogenous when promotions and demand shocks persist.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: A multi-week deal enters both the lag and current movement.
instruments.common_shocks: Chainwide promotions last more than one week.
instruments.required_controls: Pair and week effects do not create an exclusion restriction.
instruments.verdict_reason: Persistent promotions and demand shocks violate exclusion.
instruments.time_note: Previous calendar week only. A gap is not filled.

instruments.source: Other stores in the same UPC-week.
instruments.construction: Leave-one-out mean log unit price. At least two stores.
instruments.rationale: A Hausman instrument needs independent demand shocks across markets.
instruments.exclusion: One chain in one city. Promoted prices were supposed to be chainwide.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Another store's price is often the same promotion.
instruments.common_shocks: Weather, holidays, and local media hit many stores in one week.
instruments.required_controls: Separate markets. These files do not have them.
instruments.verdict_reason: Other-store prices share chainwide promotions and citywide demand.
instruments.cross_section_note: Other stores in the same UPC-week. At least two stores.
instruments.time_note: Contemporaneous. Week effects do not remove a UPC-specific chainwide price.

instruments.source: Store codebook, a 1992 snapshot of manual Part 6.
instruments.construction: Store price tier joined on store id. Not a weekly price.
instruments.rationale: Tiers summarize the chain's zone pricing.
instruments.exclusion: Tiers are pricing policy, lined up with location and Cub Foods competition.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Who lives near the store affects the tier and demand.
instruments.common_shocks: The tier does not vary over weeks.
instruments.required_controls: Pair effects absorb a time-invariant tier.
instruments.verdict_reason: A time-invariant pricing policy is not an instrument.
instruments.cross_section_note: Point-biserial correlation of a High-tier indicator with log price, on High and CubFighter rows only.
instruments.time_note: Tier is constant within every store.

instruments.construction: 1{SALE in {B, C, S}}. G and L stay unclassified.
instruments.rationale: None as an instrument. The flag is a merchandising choice.
instruments.exclusion: The manual does not describe SALE as randomized.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Features and coupons can raise movement at a given shelf price.
instruments.common_shocks: Many promotions are chainwide for one UPC.
instruments.required_controls: The confirmatory equation already uses the flag as a control.
instruments.verdict_reason: The promotion flag is an incomplete control, not an instrument.
instruments.cross_section_note: Coded B, C, or S versus blank and unclassified.
instruments.time_note: Turns on and off inside pairs. The confirmatory equation uses it as a control.

instruments.source: Kilts daily customer-count file. Sized in Phase 1 and not opened.
instruments.exclusion: Traffic is an outcome of prices and promotions.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Deals bring shoppers into the store.
instruments.common_shocks: Holidays and weather move traffic and demand together.
instruments.required_controls: Opening the file would not supply an exclusion restriction.
instruments.verdict_reason: Customer counts respond to price. They are not used.

instruments.source: Kilts 1990 store demographics. Sized in Phase 1 and not opened.
instruments.exclusion: One cross-section is absorbed by pair effects and does not shift weekly price.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Income and household composition shift demand directly.
instruments.common_shocks: None over time. The file is one cross-section.
instruments.required_controls: Store or pair fixed effects remove it.
instruments.verdict_reason: Demographics do not vary over the panel.

instruments.source: Not in the Kilts files used here.
instruments.construction: Not built. A pure weekly series is absorbed by week effects.
instruments.rationale: A national input cost could shift retail price.
instruments.exclusion: Wholesale does not imply exclusion. Week effects absorb a common weekly series.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Inflation and commodity news can move demand and costs together.
instruments.common_shocks: A national weekly index is a common shock.
instruments.required_controls: An exposure measure, if the index is to survive week effects.
instruments.verdict_reason: No cost index was joined. Week effects would absorb a pure time series.
instruments.time_note: Demonstration only: the week index is constant across rows in a week, and its remaining sum-of-squares share after week effects is 0.0.

instruments.source: Not in the Kilts files used here.
instruments.construction: Not built. No product exposure share is in the confirmatory design.
instruments.rationale: An input share can leave within-week contrast.
instruments.exclusion: Exposure must be excluded from demand. Package mix is a product attribute.
instruments.direct_demand_effects: Ingredient mix and package size enter demand directly.
instruments.common_shocks: The national factor is still common.
instruments.required_controls: No time-varying exposure is on file. Pair effects absorb a fixed share.
instruments.verdict_reason: No defensible exposure measure is in the files.

robustness.role: M5 with G and L moved into the promotion indicator.
Pair and week effects on blank SALE rows. Blank is not a confirmed regular price.
Pair and week effects on coded B/C/S rows only.
M5 on UPCs whose description begins with the discontinued mark.
M5 on UPCs without the discontinued mark.
M5 on stores coded High in the store codebook.
M5 on CubFighter stores. Few clusters make the interval rough.
M5 on weeks 201–399, which contain the 1995 gap.
M5 plus next week's log price when that week is adjacent and observed.
M5 on pairs whose unit price changes by more than $0.001.
